stemMd: A school claims that moving the first lesson later improved attendance. Which evidence most strengthens the claim?

options.label: A
options.textMd: The school repainted its classrooms the following year.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Most teachers preferred the previous timetable.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Comparable schools that kept the earlier starting time had no attendance improvement over the same period.

options.label: D
options.textMd: The later timetable contained the same subjects.

explanationMd: A contemporaneous comparison helps rule out a general trend affecting all schools. It does not prove causation by itself, but improvement concentrated in the school with the changed start time strengthens the proposed explanation.

distractorRationale.a: A later renovation does not explain the timing of attendance improvement.
distractorRationale.b: Teacher preference is not evidence about student attendance.
distractorRationale.e: This provides no comparison before and after the schedule change.
distractorRationale.d: Subject identity alone does not rule out broader attendance trends.
